name: Baltimore
operatingHours: Metro SubwayLink runs ~5:00 AM–12:00 AM weekdays and ~6:00 AM–12:00 AM weekends, every ~8 min at peak and ~15 min otherwise. Light RailLink runs ~4:00 AM–12:45 AM Mon–Sat and only ~10:00 AM–10:00 PM on Sundays and holidays, every ~15–30 min (BWI trains every 20–30 min). No overnight rail service.
fareInfo: $2.00 one-way on Metro SubwayLink, Light RailLink and local buses (2026), bought from station ticket machines or the CharmPass app; Day Pass $4.60 (valid until 3:00 AM next day), 7-day pass $22.00, also on a CharmCard. Light Rail is proof-of-payment: buy before boarding, as fines apply. The same $2.00 fare covers BWI Airport to downtown.

sights.name: National Aquarium
sights.note: A glass-pyramid aquarium on Pier 3 with a walk-through Amazon rainforest, a shark-ringed coral reef and an Australian river gorge.
sights.hours: ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM daily, later on some days in summer and on Fridays; timed entry

sights.name: Inner Harbor
sights.note: The city's waterfront basin, ringed by a brick promenade linking the aquarium, historic warships, paddle boats and harbor views.

sights.name: Fort McHenry National Monument and Historic Shrine
sights.note: The star-shaped fort whose 1814 defense against the British fleet inspired the words of the national anthem.
sights.hours: Daily, last entry 4:45 PM (fort and visitor center close shortly after); closed Thanksgiving, Dec 25, Jan 1

sights.name: Oriole Park at Camden Yards
sights.note: The retro-style home of the Orioles that set the template for modern ballparks, built against the old B&O warehouse.
sights.hours: Game days per MLB schedule; guided tours on selected days

sights.name: The Walters Art Museum
sights.note: A free museum spanning 5,000 years, from Egyptian mummies and medieval armour to a jewel-box cabinet of curiosities.
sights.hours: Wed, Fri–Sun 10:00 AM–5:00 PM; Thu 1:00–8:00 PM; closed Mon–Tue

sights.name: American Visionary Art Museum
sights.note: A joyful museum of self-taught 'outsider' artists, its mosaic-covered buildings full of whirligigs, giant sculptures and oddities.

sights.name: Fell's Point
sights.note: An 18th-century maritime village of cobbled streets, Belgian-block squares and waterfront pubs, a short water-taxi hop from the Inner Harbor.
sights.hours: Neighbourhood, always open; bars and shops keep their own hours

sights.name: Baltimore Museum of Art
sights.note: A free art museum next to Johns Hopkins with the world's largest public Matisse collection and two sculpture gardens.
sights.hours: Wed, Fri–Sun 10:00 AM–5:00 PM; Thu 10:00 AM–9:00 PM; closed Mon–Tue (reserve a free ticket)

sights.name: National Museum of Railroad History & Innovation
sights.note: The former B&O Railroad Museum, renamed in 2026, where a vast 1884 roundhouse shelters historic locomotives at the birthplace of American railroading.
sights.hours: Daily 10:00 AM–4:00 PM; campus renovation under way in phases

sights.name: George Peabody Library
sights.note: A soaring 19th-century reading room of five cast-iron balconies stacked with antique books, now run by Johns Hopkins.
sights.hours: Mon–Thu 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, Sun 11:00 AM–5:00 PM, closed Fri–Sat; check ahead, as Special Collections plans a Nov–Jan closure

sights.name: Maryland Science Center
sights.note: A hands-on science museum on the harbor with dinosaur halls, a planetarium and an IMAX dome.
sights.hours: Tue–Fri 10:00 AM–4:00 PM; Sat–Sun 10:00 AM–5:00 PM; closed Mon

sights.name: Top of the World Observation Level
sights.note: A 27th-floor deck in the pentagonal World Trade Center with 360-degree views over the harbor and skyline.
sights.hours: Wed–Thu 10:00 AM–6:00 PM; Fri–Sat 10:00 AM–7:00 PM; Sun 11:00 AM–6:00 PM; closed Mon–Tue (lease renewal pending, check ahead)

sights.name: Little Italy
sights.note: A compact enclave of rowhouse red-sauce restaurants and bakeries between the harbor and Harbor East, with outdoor films in summer.
sights.hours: Neighbourhood, always open; restaurants keep their own hours

sights.name: Edgar Allan Poe's Grave Site and Memorial
sights.note: The Westminster burying ground where Poe lies beneath a marble monument, surrounded by catacombs and 18th-century tombs.

sights.name: Federal Hill Park
sights.note: A grassy hilltop on the harbor's south shore offering the classic free panorama of the downtown skyline.

sights.name: Lexington Market
sights.note: America's oldest continuously running public market, rebuilt in 2022, famous for Faidley's crab cakes and local food stalls.
sights.hours: Mon–Wed 6:00 AM–5:00 PM; Thu–Fri 6:00 AM–6:00 PM; Sat 7:00 AM–6:00 PM; closed Sun

sights.name: Washington Monument at Mount Vernon Place
sights.note: The first major monument to George Washington, an 1829 column you can climb for views over the elegant squares of Mount Vernon.

railStations.name: Baltimore Penn Station
railStations.note: Baltimore's intercity hub: Amtrak Acela and Northeast Regional to Washington, Philadelphia and New York, plus MARC Penn Line commuter trains. The Light RailLink Penn–Camden shuttle stops outside (Mount Royal/MICA is ~0.5 km); there is no Metro SubwayLink stop. A major station renovation is under way.
railStations.hours: Station open ~5:00 AM–~1:00 AM; trains run to individual timetables.

airports.name: Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport
airports.transitNote: Light RailLink (on the map) stops at the terminal (BWI Airport station) and reaches Camden Yards and downtown in ~35 min for $2.00. A free shuttle also links the terminal to BWI Marshall Rail Station for Amtrak and MARC trains to Penn Station (~15–20 min, not on the map).
airports.hours: Light Rail: first ~4:30 AM, last ~12:00 AM Mon–Sat; Sundays ~10:00 AM–~9:30 PM.
